title: Deposing the Emperor, Dong Zhuo Installs Another; Cao Cao Presents a Sword and Flees
summary: Dong Zhuo deposes the young emperor, enthrones his nine-year-old brother as Emperor Xian, and has the mother and son poisoned. In council he answers objections by having the objector dragged out and killed.

Cao Cao takes a jewelled sword from Wang Yun and goes to Dong Zhuo's chamber to use it. Caught in the mirror's reflection, he kneels and presents the blade as a gift instead, then rides east before the story can be tested.

On the road he is sheltered by his father's sworn brother Lü Boshe, hears knives being sharpened, and kills the household — nine people — before he sees the pig tied up for the feast. He kills Lü Boshe too, on the road, to keep him from talking.
history: The sword and the mirror are the novel's. Cao Cao's flight is historical; so is a version of the killing at Lü Boshe's house, which even the sympathetic sources record.

pins.note: Fails to kill Dong Zhuo; rides east to raise an army.
Releases Cao Cao, rides with him, and leaves him after Lü Boshe.
Killed on the road with his whole household.
Lends the sword, and begins to wait.
